_comment: How a creature the world never offered arrives in one. A biome's spawn list is what may be *tried*,
not what appears -- vanilla checks the placement and the rules for every attempt -- so for almost
every creature the only question here is how often to try, and `ordinary` answers it.
The entries are the exceptions: the creatures vanilla never spawns at all, which therefore have no
Weights are against everything else the biome offers, where vanilla's monsters sit near a hundred
each. A plain mention should read as 'there are dragons here' and a rung should be able to make it an
Age *of* dragons -- so the bases are a real share of the pass rather than a curiosity. Every number
here is a first guess and wants a walk.
`apart_by` is how the big ones are kept apart: an attempt knows its position and nothing else, so a
rule about *where* is answerable where a rule about *how many* is not. One window per cell means an
Age of dragons has them spread over the country rather than seventy in one valley -- and the weight
can then be a real share, so `teeming ender_dragon` is an Age of dragons and not a curiosity.
The golems are carried past vanilla's own refusal to put a MobCategory.MISC entity in a list at all
(see SpawnerDataMixin), which is why they may be written and a datapack still may not.
`on_the_surface` and `under_the_ground` say WHERE a creature belongs, which is the thing vanilla has
no way to state: SpawnPlacements answers whether a position will hold one, never whether it ought to
be found there. Only the judgements are listed -- a creature in neither belongs anywhere, which is
vanilla's own behaviour, and one in both is a reader saying so out loud.
`placed_by_the_age` is for the two things vanilla's spawner will not do at all: it refuses a MISC
entity outright (the golems) and validates every creature against a box it must clear where it
stands, which for a dragon is 16x8 at a height vanilla never draws above the surface. Those are
taken out of the list getMobsAt builds and placed by AgeSpawner instead, at whatever ground they
belong to -- which is what `in_the_air` is for.
`apart_by` is for creatures the Age PLACES, where AgeSpawner backs it with a count of what is
already nearby. In a biome list it has no such backing: the window is one chunk of each cell, so a
creature is absent from 143 cells out of 144 and most of what spawns inside the one -- which walks
as 'they do not exist' and then 'they are everywhere'. A naturally-spawned creature is thinned by
its weight alone, which scatters it.
`by_day` and `by_night` say WHEN a creature comes, which vanilla has no notion of: its own rule is
about LIGHT, so a zombie spawns in a dark cave at noon and that is a good rule left alone. This is
for the judgement the light cannot make. Most creatures are in neither list, and a creature in both
or in neither comes at any hour. It reaches the Age's own spawner and the list vanilla is handed
alike, so a pack can give a vanilla mob hours it never had.
`in_the_light` and `in_the_dark` are the axis vanilla DOES have, and are here because not everything
is subject to it: a monster's checkSpawnRules tests the light and a golem's does not, and a creature
the Age places rather than offers has no rule run over it at all. A creature in neither list keeps
whatever vanilla would have decided.
